item: A full-suite run as root no longer turns /dev/null into a regular file, and the plan and out-of-memory tests pass on SQLite 3.53.1 as well as the older one
summary: First full-suite run on a second SQLite (3.53.1; 28338 passed, 5 failed, 120 skipped, 5749 s). Three tests used Path(os.devnull) as a DamageRegistry store: the registry os.replace-s its record over its store, which a non-root user cannot do in /dev (swallowed) and root can, so a root run left /dev/null a regular file holding the registry JSON and a distant test (stdin=DEVNULL) read it. The stores are tmp_path files; a new last-sorting file scans tests/ and src/ for os.devnull and the whole string /dev/null as a path (allowlist with reasons, stale entries fail), proves with a unix socket that the registry replaces any node at its store path, and fails if /dev/null is not a character device at the end. test_browse_plan reads the meaning of a tie-only sort (RIGHT PART, LAST TERM, LAST n TERMS) instead of SQLite's words and proves its helper on the running library; the FTS5 out-of-memory test accepts the row and the empty-MemoryError shapes and keeps the verdict strictly unchecked. Product code unchanged. Mutants: PENDING.
